newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Light raises rates average 5.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: China Light raises rates average 5.9 pct.

text.p: China Light & Power Co Ltd announced on Tuesday an average increase in electricity prices of 5.9 percent, or 2.3 cents per unit, over the weighted average of last year's tariffs, effective from March 1.
It said domestic customers consuming 500 units would pay HK$0.85 more and 1,000 units HK$12.50 more per month.
Among its 1.5 million domestic customers, China Light said more than 75 percent, or 1.1 million who consume 415 units or less a month, would experience no increase in March.
The rise was necessary "simply to cope with higher operating and capital costs as a result of inflation", Jimmy Lui, general manager, distribution and customer services, told reporters.
China Light said basic tariffs would increase by 3.5 cents per unit, but a transfer from the Development Fund would allow a special rebate of 1.2 cents per unit to partly offset the rise.

"Although sales growth has been slower than expected in recent years, and revenue correspondingly reduced, we have again managed to maintain our net average tariff at a level lower than the projected tariff contained in the 1992-1999 Financing Plan, which was approved by the government," managing director Ross Sayers said in a statement.
The last time the Hong Kong utility increased its tariffs was March 1, 1996, when prices were raised by 6.7 percent over the weighted average of the previous year.
